Samir — great questions. Short answers and operational detail below.

On Tue, Sep 12, 2026 at 11:27 AM Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Canary window: are the rollback gates based on latency/error budget only, or do you include qualitative checks (sampled transcript review) at each ramp step?

We always combine automated SLO gates with manual quality checks at key ramps. Proposed guardrails: 
- Automated: 95th p50 latency, token error rate (exceptions / total requests) must remain within agreed thresholds during the 30-minute stabilization window after each ramp.
- Manual QC: sample 25 sessions (stratified by route) for quality & hallucination checks at the 10% and 50% ramps. Engineering + your SME should sign-off before moving to the next step.

On training: for an 18-person ops team we recommend: 
- Cohort A (hands-on): 8-10 people (operators + 2 super-users) — live lab exercises and incident drills.
- Cohort B (observers + product): 8-10 people — overview + Q&A.

Also attaching the internal canary runbook and rollback checklist for your review. The runbook includes exact Prometheus + tracing dashboards and slack alert thresholds we will monitor.

Attachment: [Attachment: Canary_Runbook.md (Markdown, 42KB)]

Happy to walk through the runbook during the kickoff workshop.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
